Either way it is after the window. The in-window events are the late-October hyperscaler Q3 prints and their 2027 capex remarks (Microsoft 26% and Meta 16% of Arista's FY2025 revenue). bear.story: 2027 capex digestion at Microsoft/Meta (42% of revenue), or white-box share gains in 1.6T: Celestica starts 1.6T mass production with two hyperscalers in Q3 2026, ahead of Arista's Q4 2026 first shipments (src 20-21). Either cuts 2027-28 growth to low teens. The $9.6B purchase commitments turn into inventory risk, rising DRAM/NAND costs (+10-20% QoQ in 4Q26, src 23) squeeze gross margin below 62%, and the multiple falls to ~25x on ~$5.5-6 NTM EPS.

base.story: FY26 lands at ~$12.7B+ and FY27 grows ~28% to ~$16.3B on consensus EPS of $5.20. Supplier signals (Broadcom AI networking >2.5x YoY, Q4 AI guide $21.7B) and purchase commitments covering chip shipments into Q3 2027 support delivery. The $6.87B deferred revenue converts as acceptance hits. EPS growth of ~25% is mostly offset by de-rating from ~41x to ~34-35x NTM EPS of ~$6.0-6.2.

bull.story: Supply eases and the deferred backlog converts, pushing 2027 revenue toward $17-18B. A third and fourth 10% customer appear, as management anticipates (src 22), easing concentration. The 1.6T 7060XE7 ramps in H1 2027 and scale-up Ethernet optionality for 2028 keeps the multiple near ~40x on $6.5-7 NTM EPS.

thesis_break_reason: $140 is ~31% below spot and ~23x my Sep-2027 NTM EPS (~27x FY27 consensus of $5.20), well under the ~34x five-year average forward multiple. It is also below the May-2026 post-Q1 selloff lows of ~$136-142. A move there most likely means something fundamental: a Microsoft/Meta capex cut, a large customer shifting 1.6T back-end to white-box or Nvidia, a guide-down, or deferred revenue unwinding. At 40-54% vol, ordinary noise around a ~$206 value doesn't usually get there.

reasoning: Round 2. Facts corrected per the supervisor: consensus FY26/FY27 EPS is $4.11/$5.20 (up 16% in 60 days); cash is $13.34B reported, and my ~$19.5B is a labelled Sep-2027 projection; Q3 is unannounced and likely Tue Nov 3; the analyst day was Sep 2025, not November. I dropped the alt-data the supervisor discounted (Reddit percentile, job boards, X snippet, Manifold N/A), so none of it drives a number. In its place I added supply-chain evidence from my lane. (1) Supplier data: Broadcom, Arista's main merchant-silicon supplier, grew AI networking over 2.5x YoY and guided AI revenue to $21.7B for Q4. Arista's reported revenue grew ~38% and IDC branded DC Ethernet grew ~65%, which fits the view that Arista's gap is partly shipment and acceptance timing (deferred $6.87B; Dell'Oro says 'more closely tied' including deferred) and partly real share loss. (2) Competitor channel: Celestica began 1.6T mass production with two hyperscalers in Q3 2026 and says 2027 growth will exceed 2026's ~65%. Arista's 1.6T 7060XE7 only starts shipping in Q4 2026. That is a concrete white-box head start in the next generation and a real bear input. (3) Lead time and visibility: purchase commitments are $9.6B, up from $3.6B three quarters ago, and cover chip shipments into Q3 2027. That gives supply visibility for the forecast year but inventory risk if demand pauses. (4) Cost tracker: TrendForce's Sep 30 forecast has DRAM +10-15% and NAND +15-20% QoQ in 4Q26, a headwind to the 62-64% GM target. Net: the positives (visibility, supplier demand) and negatives (1.6T white-box lead, memory costs) roughly offset. I raise the P/E to 34.5x from 34x and use consensus $5.20, so fair value moves $205 to $206, just below the supervisor's $209. I don't go to $209 because the Celestica 1.6T head start and memory inflation argue against the FCF-yield upside. The ladder is a three-scenario lognormal mixture: bear $150 (25%, sigma 0.40), base $214 (50%, sigma 0.28), bull $278 (25%, sigma 0.30). That gives a median ~$211 and P(>=204) ~55%. No option data was used. Research was limited to ~7 extra queries.
